findings.claim: The dedicated selector cannot rehydrate or apply production workshop materials because it reads each material through `id` while the real catalog emits `materialId`. The current choice never highlights; clicking a card stores the literal string `undefined`; Apply sends that value; and the main dialog normalizes it back to the first allowed material, reproducing the reported no-change behavior in both directions.
proof_refs: backend-go/internal/api/furniture_catalog.go:84-101 serializes workshop materials with json key materialId, and apps/sketchup-extension/src/granete_for_sketchup/library/catalog_provider.rb:213-220 passes that contract through unchanged.
material_selector.html:757,1023-1033,1051-1067 exclusively read mat.id/m.id; template interpolation turns the missing property into data-id="undefined".
dialog.html:1971-1974 uses the correct materialId key; dialog.html:2043-2046 rejects `undefined` and rewrites the choice to availableIds[0] before dialog.html:3143-3151 sends the update.

option_selector_controller_test.rb:17-23 and :39-56 fabricate selector fixtures with `id`, while remote_catalog_provider_test.rb:289-315 proves the production payload uses `materialId`; no test executes the selector JavaScript against the production contract.

findings.claim: The secondary selector ignores the selected furniture role's curated optionIds and exposes every active workshop board. When a user chooses a material outside that role, the main dialog silently replaces it with the first allowed option yet shows a success toast naming the rejected choice, so a core material workflow is both invalid and deceptive.
proof_refs: dialog.html:2035-2047 computes the role-specific availableIds, but dialog.html:2095-2101 sends only role, roleName and currentMaterialId to Ruby.
dialog_controller.rb:170-188 supplies @catalog_provider.all_materials without filtering by the definition role's optionIds.

dialog.html:3124-3167 writes the returned ID, rerenders through the role validator (which resets unsupported IDs at :2044-2046), then reports success using the originally returned material at :3154-3155.
backend-go/internal/api/furniture_catalog.go:69-81 and :280-311 define materialRoles.optionIds as the workshop-curated role contract.

findings.claim: The selector advertises a project-default scope, but the receiving callback never reads payload.scope and always mutates either the current furniture or the insertion draft. Selecting 'Valor por defecto de la obra' therefore cannot update project defaults and silently performs a different operation.
proof_refs: material_selector.html:662-671 exposes furniture/project scope and :1110-1120 serializes the selected scope.
option_selector_controller.rb:99-106 and dialog_controller.rb:190-195 preserve scope across the HtmlDialog bridge.
dialog.html:3124-3168 reads only role/materialId and contains no scope branch or project-default persistence path.

The retained in-dialog selector uses the same unsupported `project` token at dialog.html:1715-1724, while docs/architecture/catalog-option-selector.md:261-270 specifies selected_furniture, selected_component and project_default.

findings.claim: A remote layout failure is treated as a valid generic-layout request. During update, the plugin clears the existing furniture's complete component/hardware hierarchy, replaces it with an invented two-side parametric approximation, persists the requested metadata, and returns success instead of preserving the model and surfacing the 4xx/5xx/network error.
proof_refs: catalog_provider.rb:236-247 and :327-343 collapse authentication, license, validation, server, network and invalid-body failures to nil.
dialog_controller.rb:101-111 calls update_furniture even when resolve_layout_for returned nil.
furniture_builder.rb:114-140 clears group.entities before rendering, and :159-166 maps nil to render_generic_parametric_layout while still returning success.

docs/architecture/sketchup-interaction-model.md:158-160 and :169-190 require explicit 422 behavior and say an unknown/inactive material must never silently fall back; remote_catalog_provider_test.rb:250-275 only asserts nil and never proves the model is not mutated.

findings.claim: Stale or missing furniture identity is not fail-closed: a missed instance lookup falls back to the first selected entity and clears/rebuilds it, while a missing target reports mock success. Because the selection observer is attached only to the model active when the dialog opens and is never moved on active-model changes, switching SketchUp documents provides a deterministic path to overwriting an unrelated group in the new model or claiming an update that never happened.
proof_refs: dialog_controller.rb:117-129 returns search_entities_for_instance(instance_id) || first even when first's metadata does not match; :101-114 returns mock_result when no target exists.
furniture_builder.rb:114-125 immediately clears whichever group is returned and rewrites its metadata.

dialog_controller.rb:230-239 and :398-404 add/remove the observer only through the current active_model selection; lifecycle.rb:68-83 implements only onUnloadExtension and no onActivateModel reattachment/rehydration.
selection_observer_test.rb and application_test.rb:145-183 cover one model only; no active-model switch or stale-instance rejection test exists.

findings.claim: Workshop catalog strings are inserted into innerHTML without escaping inside a privileged HtmlDialog that also receives the bearer media token. A stored material/category name or visual URL containing markup can execute script, read state.media.token, invoke SketchUp callbacks, or exfiltrate the 30-day extension credential.
proof_refs: material_selector.html:832-837,858-874,894-951 and :1022-1049 interpolate category IDs/names, material name/code/manufacturer, colors and URLs directly into innerHTML/style attributes; the document has no Content-Security-Policy.
dialog_controller.rb:354-367 puts the raw bearer token in the selector payload, and material_selector.html:727-734 stores it in script-visible state.
backend-go/internal/api/furniture_catalog.go:238-275 projects database strings directly into the catalog without HTML encoding.
dialog_controller_test.rb:251-269 explicitly confirms token injection; no hostile catalog-string browser test exists.

findings.claim: Material updates are rendered locally and announced as successful before Ruby acknowledges persistence; onUpdateResult reports an error but never rolls back or rehydrates the prior materialChoices. Any builder/bridge failure leaves the main UI and the next selector seed claiming a finish that the SketchUp furniture does not contain.
proof_refs: dialog.html:3124-3155 mutates inspectorMaterialChoices, rerenders, sends update_furniture, and immediately shows a success toast.
dialog.html:3065-3075 only reenables the button and shows an error on failure; it does not restore choices or request current selection metadata.
dialog.html:2095-2101 seeds a reopened selector from the locally held choices object.

findings.claim: Delete erases the first selected SketchUp entity without verifying that it is the furniture instance shown by the inspector and without confirmation. Selection races or stale cross-model UI can therefore delete an unrelated entity; Undo may recover it, but the command itself is not identity-safe.
proof_refs: dialog_controller.rb:373-381 reads active_model.selection.first and directly calls erase_entities without metadata/instanceRef validation.
dialog.html:3492-3497 dispatches deletion without confirmation or an instanceId payload.
No deletion target-safety test appears in dialog_controller_test.rb, application_test.rb, or selection_observer_test.rb.

findings.claim: Catalog freshness is broken in both layers: the plugin caches the first successful catalog forever until login/logout, and the backend revision/ETag omits materialCategories. Material edits made in Granete during a SketchUp session cannot be refreshed, and category-only changes can retain the same revision.
proof_refs: catalog_provider.rb:260-270 always returns @cached_contract once populated; reset at :249-255 is called only around login/logout in dialog_controller.rb:34-49.
The get_catalog callback at dialog_controller.rb:304-319 calls send_catalog but cannot bypass that cache.

backend-go/internal/api/furniture_catalog.go:431-448 hashes Categories, Definitions, Presets and Materials but not c.MaterialCategories, although furniture.go:103-117 uses that revision as the response ETag.
furniture_catalog_test.go:130-143 tests other revision content and does not cover a material-category-only change.

findings.claim: Texture caching can render the wrong finish and can be abused for unbounded client-side fetches: the cache key is only the URL basename, so distinct materials collide, while any absolute HTTP(S) host is downloaded with no origin allowlist, size limit, content-type check, or atomic write.
proof_refs: texture_cache.rb:30-39 derives local_path solely from File.basename and permanently reuses any positive-size file.
texture_cache.rb:55-79 accepts arbitrary absolute URLs and File.binwrite's the full response body without validating content or bounding bytes.
texture_cache_test.rb:51-64 tests only blank and already-cached paths; collisions, hostile URLs, oversized bodies and partial writes are untested.

findings.claim: Credential transport and storage are not hardened: explicit http:// server URLs are accepted and carry login passwords/bearer tokens in plaintext, while the 30-day bearer token is written with default filesystem permissions and a non-atomic overwrite.
proof_refs: http_adapter.rb:62-71 accepts URI::HTTP and build_http at :81-86 disables TLS for an HTTP URI.
session_provider.rb:40-47 posts email/password through that adapter and :63-78 uses the bearer header on subsequent requests.
session_provider.rb:165-193 uses FileUtils.mkdir_p and File.write without an explicit 0700 directory, 0600 file mode, temp-file+rename, or platform credential store.
README.md:49-58 documents a 30-day bearer credential, increasing the impact of local disclosure or plaintext transport.

findings.claim: The dedicated selector is mouse-dependent and does not meet its own keyboard/accessibility contract: categories, breadcrumbs and material cards are clickable divs with no roles, tabindex, accessible names, selected state, arrow-key behavior, or focus-visible treatment; only global Enter/Escape are implemented.
proof_refs: material_selector.html:832-849,858-967 and :1022-1063 create span/div controls and attach click/dblclick handlers only; the entire document contains no aria-* or tabindex attributes.
material_selector.html:1155-1165 implements Escape, Enter and Cmd/Ctrl-F but no ArrowLeft/Right/Up/Down navigation.
docs/architecture/catalog-option-selector.md:318-331 requires directional keyboard navigation and disabled incompatible candidates.
dialog.html:1396-1405 declares tabs but switchTab at :1911-1919 never updates aria-selected, aria-controls or roving tabindex; neither dialog declares an aria-live region for feedback.

findings.claim: The new selector forks the plugin's visual system and does not adapt to constrained windows: it introduces a separate hard-coded dark cyan palette beside the main light indigo token system, fixes a Miller/grid/300px inspector layout with no media queries, uses 10-11px secondary text, and leaves Apply visually enabled even when no candidate exists.
proof_refs: material_selector.html:8-27 defines a standalone hex palette; dialog.html:8-65 defines the established light/brand token system.

material_selector.html:176-205 fixes the three-zone grid and 150-160px Miller columns plus a 300px inspector; no @media or prefers-reduced-motion rule exists in that file, while option_selector_controller.rb:62-72 permits resizing down to 760x500.
material_selector.html:676-680 renders Apply enabled at startup, while applySelection at :1110-1112 silently returns with no selection.
dialog.html:1626-1736 and :2121-2595 retain an entire second hidden selector implementation with different copy/behavior, adding cognitive and maintenance debt.

findings.claim: Operator documentation and in-product status copy describe behavior the production wiring does not provide: they promise an offline/local fallback and null default ports, but production always constructs a real SessionProvider/HttpAdapter plus a RemoteCatalogProvider with no fallback and returns an empty catalog when unavailable.
proof_refs: README.md:59-64 promises local fallback, and :124-132 says both defaults are null implementations; README.md:50 also misspells the client claim as sketchetchup-extension.
application.rb:15-26 constructs SessionProvider and RemoteCatalogProvider without fallback_provider.
catalog_provider.rb:143-151 and :179-223 explicitly return an empty catalog unless an explicit fallback was injected.

application.rb:80-87 repeats the false offline-fallback promise in user-facing connection status copy, while docs/architecture/sketchup-interaction-model.md:111-118 states the actual fail-closed behavior.

findings.claim: The hardware asset pipeline is dead in production: every resolved handle/hinge/rail is rendered as a colored box, the AssetLoader is never called or injected, and the resolver cannot perform the documented remote download. This prevents visually accurate supported hardware despite the documented 3D-asset hierarchy.
proof_refs: furniture_builder.rb:79-82 accepts asset_loader but render_resolved_hardware at :211-221 always creates box geometry and never references @asset_loader or hardware identity/shape.
dialog_controller.rb:269-278 constructs FurnitureBuilder with only metadata_store and texture_cache.
asset_resolver.rb:14-21 checks bundle/cache only, and asset_loader.rb:11-30 supports translation only; asset_loader_test.rb:14-24 covers only missing assets.
docs/architecture/sketchup-interaction-model.md:99-107 promises cache, bundle, remote download and generic fallback for unavailable .skp assets.

findings.claim: Furniture persistence does not carry real project or source revision identity: every model receives the same projectRef and every insert/update writes sourceRevisionRef `rev-1`. Cross-session synchronization, stale detection and project-level material defaults therefore have no trustworthy identity anchor.
proof_refs: furniture_builder.rb:313-334 hard-codes project-sketchup-active and rev-1 for all furniture; :337-347 repeats the project constant for components.
generate_instance_id at furniture_builder.rb:145-147 is random and has no collision check.

docs/sketchup-manufacturing-contract.md:123-161 requires explicit project/source revision correlation and says projectId must not be inferred; packages/domain/src/sketchupAuthoringSchema.ts:106-122 models those fields as required envelope identity.
metadata_store_test.rb:109-114 asserts only that host entity IDs are not used; it does not test real project/revision rehydration or revision advancement.

evidence: Confirmed all 101 manifest paths were inspected through read-only Git object/tree commands; every manifest blob OID matched commit:path (101 matched, 0 mismatches), including both PNG headers, Ruby/HTML source, all plugin tests/configuration, Go API/layout code and tests, shared JSON contract, seven architecture/strategy documents, and TypeScript domain code/tests.

Reported material defect was traced end-to-end in both directions: main dialog choice -> currentMaterialId -> Ruby selector payload -> selector rehydration, and selector card -> materialId bridge -> main choices -> Ruby update -> metadata/model rendering.
